title: The verse passed on
hook: Upatissa hears Assaji's verse, understands, and runs to tell Kolita (Vinaya, Mahavagga 1)

segments.voice: Yesterday: a pact. Whoever reaches the deathless first will tell the other, and your line, whoever finds it first. Today, one of them finds it.

Kolita sees his friend coming from a distance, and something has already changed. Not a word has been said. It's in Upatissa's face. The Vinaya, the monks' book of discipline, tells it simply: Kolita sees that his friend looks calm and clear, and asks him straight out whether he has found the deathless, the thing they both left home to look for. And Upatissa says yes. Earlier on this path we followed Upatissa behind a quiet monk named Assaji and heard the short verse Assaji gave him. Today is the other half of that morning: what Upatissa did with it.
screen: `A CHANGED FACE.` → `HAVE YOU FOUND IT?` → `YES, FRIEND.`

segments.voice: Start with where he went. Upatissa had just understood the thing he left home to look for. He could have stayed to question Assaji, or gone straight to find the Buddha. Instead he went to Kolita, because that was the pact. The verse was small enough to carry at a run. In paraphrase: of things that arise from a cause, the Buddha has told the cause, and also how they cease. Next, what he passed on. Not his own summary. Not a better version. He gave Kolita the same lines he'd heard, and the text says that on hearing them, Kolita understood too. Then they thought of someone else. Their old teacher, Sanjaya, still led a crowd of students, so the two went back and invited him to come with them. He refused, and offered instead to share the leadership of his group. They said no to that and left, and the Vinaya says many of his students went with them. Last, the arrival. The text says the Buddha saw the two friends coming from far off and told the monks, in paraphrase: these two will be my chief pair of disciples. Upatissa would be called Sariputta, and Kolita, Moggallana. Here's what the story keeps doing. Everyone in it who finds something good turns around and hands it on. Assaji to Upatissa. Upatissa to Kolita. Both of them to their old teacher. The verse travels because nobody sits on it.
screen: `HE WENT TO KOLITA FIRST.` · `THE SAME VERSE, UNCHANGED.` · `BACK TO THE OLD TEACHER.` · `THE CHIEF PAIR ARRIVES.` · then, large: `HE RAN TO TELL HIM.`

segments.voice: Find one thing from the last week that helped you, a sentence someone said, a song, a recipe that worked, and bring to mind the face of the person who would want it. Don't polish it or add to it; just hold the two together, the gift and the friend, and rest with the breath.
Deathless. The thing Upatissa tells Kolita he has found, after hearing Assaji's short verse and understanding it. Today's word.
Your line: he ran to tell him. The same verse, unchanged, from one friend to the next. Day seven hundred twenty-seven.

screen: `DAY 727 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE GENERAL OF THE DHAMMA.`

howItsDone: Assaji's verse is recited in Buddhist communities as a summary of the teaching, and the story of the two friends is told at temples and in Dhamma talks as the beginning of the Buddha's chief pair of disciples.

original.note: Pali: 'the things that arise from a cause', the opening words of Assaji's verse.

trapdoor: what you thought: a story about one famous verse.
what it means: the verse works twice. Upatissa hears it from Assaji, gives the same words to Kolita, and it works again.
what a scholar hears: in the Vinaya the story sits in the opening narrative of the Mahavagga, which tells how the order of monks first grew.

chat.says: When Upatissa found what he was looking for, what did he do first?
options: He ran to Kolita, as they'd promised, and gave him the same verse.
He went straight to the Buddha and stayed there to learn more.
He wrote the verse out in his own words to make it clearer.
chat.meaning: Because of the pact he went first to Kolita, passing on Assaji's verse unchanged, and Kolita understood too.

Assaji.meaning: a quiet monk who gave Upatissa a short verse

Sanjaya.meaning: the friends' old teacher, a wanderer in Rajagaha

sources.ref: Vinaya Pitaka, Mahavagga 1.23–24 (Sariputta and Moggallana: the verse, the pact kept, Sanjaya, the arrival)

notes: All Vinaya material paraphrased. Confirm in Mahavagga 1.23–24 (Rhys Davids and Oldenberg, SBE 13): Moggallana notices Sariputta's serene face and asks whether he has reached the deathless; Sariputta repeats Assaji's verse and Moggallana understands; they invite Sanjaya, who refuses and offers to share leadership; Sanjaya's students go with them; the Buddha sees them from afar and names them his chief pair.
Script says 'many of his students' rather than the number the Vinaya gives (two hundred fifty), per the claims rule; the text's own number could be restored if wanted.
The Vinaya also says Sanjaya vomited hot blood when his students left; omitted as needlessly harsh for this angle.
Day 68 (year one) told the Assaji meeting itself and the verse's spread in inscriptions; this day deliberately takes the second half of the morning instead.
Original: confirm Devanagari and the transliteration 'ye dhamma hetuppabhava'; stress marking is approximate.
Editor: cut 'spent years chasing' (unsupported duration), replaced 'good news' with neutral wording, and fixed the garbled practice line about Kolita seeing his friend's face.
